note: Realistic animal models (Dave 6 Nov 2026: aim for photorealism; design/realistic_animals_plan.md, src/client/animal_view.gd _make_model). A species row here whose scene exists is drawn from that rigged, animated scene instead of the code-built body; no row or a missing file keeps the code body. Row: scene (res:// path of a .glb/.fbx/.tscn), scale, yaw_deg (turn so the animal faces -Z), walk_mps and run_mps (ground speeds the walk and run clips were made at), stride_m (metres per footstep), clips {state number or 'walk'/'run': clip name}; states 0 graze, 1 hop, 2 flee, 3 alert, 10 warn, 11 charge, 12 recover, 16 the jaw-pop warning (bears; falls back to 10). Example: "bear": {"scene": "res://assets/animals/bear/bear.glb", "scale": 1.0, "yaw_deg": 180, "walk_mps": 1.3, "run_mps": 9.0, "stride_m": 1.1, "clips": {"0": "Eat", "3": "Idle", "10": "Roar", "11": "Run", "12": "Idle", "walk": "Walk", "run": "Run"}}. clip_prefix (optional) is put before every clip name; without it a clip is found by its name after the armature ('Armature|Idle' answers 'Idle'). The model files are bought (WildMesh 3D Ultimate 3D Animal Pack, Dave 6 Nov 2026) and are NOT in git (/assets/animals/ is ignored): copy them from the pack into assets/animals/<kind>/ on a build machine. length_m: the model is scaled so its longest side is this long (any file units). materials: [{match, albedo, tint (optional [r, g, b] the texture is multiplied by)} or {match, hide: true}] colour textures set in code, first matching entry per surface (match '' = the rest). length_m values: design/wildmesh_scale_table.md (real adult length, nose to tail tip). Species added 7 Nov (deer, moose, boar, wolf, fox, rabbit): yaw, clip speeds and material matches are first guesses from the bear; the shot runner --shot-animals row checks them. pack (optional): the model's folder inside the bought pack; tools/install_animal_models.py copies it into the scene's folder (no .blend: headless import cannot read it). size_clip (optional): size and ground the model by its bones in that clip's first frame, for a file whose imported pose is not standing. bounds: mesh sizes by the skinned mesh instead of the bones. young_model (optional): a young animal of this species is drawn from this model at its own size (keys laid over the row like a variant) instead of the adult shrunk to half. flock_of [min, max] (optional): one record is a flock of that many birds built from the model, spread over spread_m, set sink_m into the surface. flat_share (optional, default 0.5): a clip is refused as flat below this share of the standing height; lower it for an upright animal that bends low to eat. bone_offsets (optional): {bone: [x, y, z] degrees in the bone's own axes} turned after every clip (src/client/bone_offsets.gd), to correct a pose the clips hold. clip_loop (optional): {role: [t0, t1, blend_s]} loops that window of the role's clip, its last blend_s seconds eased back to the first pose (tools/find_loop.gd finds the window). gait (optional): {role: {period_s, bones {bone: [phase, swing degrees, axis]}}} builds a looping clip for that role from the model's own bones (_gait_clip). sink_share (flock rows): sink by that share of the bird's height in its graze clip. strike, strike2, kick (optional clip roles, played once): a close blow (server_big_game STRIKE, two strikes taking turns) and a kick behind (KICK), each sped so its blow lands when the server's does (animals.json defend strike/kick windup_s); hit_at (optional, default 0.45): where in those clips the blow lands, as a share of the clip.

bear.note: WildMesh BrownBear (Realistic Animals/BrownBear/SK_Bear.fbx, textures in its Textures folder): 7508 triangles, 35 bones, 81 clips; faces +Z, so yaw 180. Alert stands up on its hind legs; warn stands up on its hind legs too (Dave 25 Nov 2026: a threatened bear stands its ground and rears up first, then attacks with claws or bite; it was the angry breathing stance); charge sprints. Jaw-pop (state 16, Steve #600): Attack_IdleAngry_01_Low, a low angry swat. The black bear is drawn from this model, darkened (its own file has no stand-up or attack clips; see its row).
bear.variants_note: Coordinator 26 Nov 2026, Lane A pictures pr_bearclose_rear at 96ec6be0: the bear_2 look (WildMesh Bear) has no clip that stands on its hind legs in time (its warn Attack_StandAngry_01_Low is a low crouch; its StandHind clips sit on the haunches, as the black bear's pictures of 25 Nov showed), so it is no longer drawn: Dave 26 Nov 2026, up close a bear should "turn rear on its hind legs growl and fight". Every brown bear is this look, which rears (IdleHind_Idle_01), jaw-pops (16) and has its strikes and bite. A look's clips replace the row's whole clips, so each look names every role it plays.

goblin.note: Goblins (Dave 7 Nov 2026, docs/GOBLINS.md). alligator.note: Dave's Alligator_Al.glb (27 Nov 2026): its clips are borrowed from cats, a dog, a fox and a leopard. Dave: "ignore the dog walk its terrible", so Walking is never used: walk is cat_walk, the run and charge the dog's Running, the bite the leopard's pounce (feipu), the strike its tail swipe (shuaiwei), the death leopard_dead; stand, alert and warn the fox idle (cat_idle2 is 3.04 times its flat rest height, over TALL_SHARE, so only an idle variant if ever). The lie is its own rest pose, belly and tail flat (gait 19 rest_all; the cat sleep curled it into a ball, Lane A 27 Nov). No swim or hit clip: in water it plays its state's clip. tail_drag (src/client/tail_drag.gd) lays the tail on the ground over every clip (Dave: "all the actions need to let the tail drag on the ground"). crawl (src/client/crawl.gd) lets the body down level to its rest height and bends the legs out to the sides with the feet where the clip put them, in the idle, walk, bite and strike (Dave 27 Nov: "bend his legs more like a real alligator and slow down his walk so he crawls"; the run stays a high walk); the bite and strike (flat) also lay the spine from the hips to the head at its rest slope and keep the feet on the ground (28 Nov: the leopard's pounce and tail swipe hunched it like a cat); the server walks it at 0.4 m/s (animals.json), cat_walk's feet move 0.47 m/s. ground_m and ground_clips come from skinning the file off line with the tail laid down and the body let down (thread, 27 Nov): tools/ground_check.gd poses the raw clips, whose cat and fox tails dip through the ground, so its lowest points for this model are the tail's, not the feet's.
